text:
ashley (sec-eng): DAST bubbled a high-severity auth bypass on the SSO callback endpoint in staging. stacktrace attached but looks like a 302 -> 200 chain that shouldn't allow access. anyone else seeing similar?

sam (backend): saw an alert earlier too. we did a keystore RBAC tweak yesterday to let the scan runner read a testing key. could be related.

ashley (sec-eng): @sam that RBAC change was the `scanner-read` binding? logs show a `principal: scan-runner@infra` granted `roles/keystore.viewer` around 11:03.

sam (backend): yep that's the one. intended to be scoped to staging-only but might have leaked to the test callback. i rolled a tighter policy at 12:10 but not sure if DAST hit during the window.

kevin (infra): quick audit query you can run: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy" AND resource.labels.project_id="redwood-staging"' --freshness=2h` should show the binding change event and actor.

mike (oncall): we're getting pages about 403s to keystore from the preview cluster since ~11:05. seems correlated.

ashley (sec-eng): sec-bot uploaded the DAST report: https://dast.internal/reports/4823456789 — note the reproduction step: `POST /auth/callback?state=...` with a forged state header. stack shows the session created even though subject was unauth.

sam (backend): my guess: the scan runner used a test service account that was accidentally added to `keystore.viewer` and we accidentally accepted the `state` param for test-mode sessions. two issues.

ashley (sec-eng): immediate ask: can we revoke the `scanner` binding and rotate the ephemeral key used by the runner? also need to preserve audit logs for IR.

kevin (infra): done — revoked binding at 12:30 and initiated KMS key rotation job `rot-job-2024-4823`. rotation id: `rot-4823`. command used: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/kr/staging-key`

mike (oncall): copying timeline to incident channel and silencing pages for the preview cluster. if the DAST repro still works after revocation, we'll treat as vuln not RBAC.

ashley (sec-eng): @sam can you run a quick canary: repro the POST from an external IP (not scan-runner) and confirm response is 401/302 (not 200)? paste curl: ```curl -v -X POST 'https://staging.redwood/api/auth/callback' -d 'state=fake' -H 'Cookie: _session=none'```

sam (backend): running now. quick log: `2024-05-14T12:45:12Z auth: callback rejected principal=unknown -> 401`. appears fixed after revocation. will run the full suite in 10m.

ashley (sec-eng): good. follow-ups: 1) tighten pre-merge review for any RBAC changes (PR checklist item) 2) update scanner runbooks so they request ephemeral grants via the `scanner-orchestrator` 3) preserve DAST evidence in the IR ticket.

kevin (infra): agreed. i'll add audithook to forward keystore IAM events to the security S3 bucket for 90 days (was 30). PR incoming.

sec-bot: automated note — ticket created: INC-2024-234 (security triage), severity: P2. attached DAST report and `SetIamPolicy` audit entries.

mike (oncall): marking incident resolved for paging; keeping triage open until IR checklist completed. :white_check_mark:

ashley (sec-eng): will file a short postmortem focusing on the human step (scoped RBAC change without explicit expiration) + tooling gaps. assigning action items in the ticket. thanks team. :pray:
